# Results (generated by `python -m brainguard.report`; do not edit by hand)

Confidence intervals: 95%, patient-level bootstrap (2,000 draws). p-values in the hypothesis table are Holm-adjusted across that table.

## Main model: EfficientNetB0, figshare, patient-grouped 5-fold CV

3,064 images from 233 patients; every prediction is for a patient the model never saw.

| Metric | Value (95% CI) |
|---|---|
| Accuracy | 88.4% (85.5%–91.1%) |
| Balanced accuracy | 86.5% (83.5%–89.1%) |
| Macro F1 | 0.865 (0.833–0.892) |
| Macro one-vs-rest AUC | 0.971 (0.951–0.985) |
| Cohen's κ | 0.818 |
| Calibration: ECE / Brier | 0.045 / 0.170 |
| Accuracy across folds | 88.4% ± 1.6% (SD) |

| Class | Images | Sensitivity | Specificity | Precision | AUC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| glioma | 1,426 | 91.2% (87.6%–94.6%) | 92.7% (89.8%–95.1%) | 91.6% (87.3%–94.8%) | 0.981 (0.971–0.989) |
| meningioma | 708 | 69.9% (62.0%–77.5%) | 95.2% (93.1%–97.1%) | 81.3% (72.6%–88.6%) | 0.941 (0.899–0.971) |
| pituitary | 930 | 98.3% (96.2%–99.8%) | 94.3% (91.5%–96.6%) | 88.2% (82.0%–93.0%) | 0.990 (0.974–0.998) |

## Hypothesis tests

| # | Hypothesis | Evidence | p (Holm) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H4 | Meningioma is detected less reliably than the other classes | sensitivity difference -24.1% (CI -32.3% to -16.4%) | 0.002 | supported |
| H1 | Image-level CV overstates accuracy versus patient-level CV (leakage) | balanced accuracy 91.6% (effnet_image) vs 86.5% (main); McNemar 201/49 discordant | 2.9e-22 | supported |
| H2 | Transfer learning (EfficientNetB0) beats the baseline CNN | balanced accuracy 87.2% (cnn_patient) vs 86.5% (main); McNemar 171/173 discordant | 1 | not supported |
| H3 | Class weighting improves balanced accuracy | balanced accuracy 87.6% (effnet_patient_cw) vs 86.5% (main); McNemar 73/55 discordant | 0.4 | not supported |
| H5a | Kaggle accuracy is higher when the image has a near-copy in Training | 99.3% vs 93.7% | 2.7e-08 | supported |
| H5b | Kaggle accuracy is higher when the image's patient is in Training | 97.7% vs 96.6% | 1 | not supported |
| H6 | SHAP attribution concentrates on the tumour more than chance | median 3.5% inside vs 1.2% area | 9.5e-25 | supported |

## Kaggle benchmark as published (4 classes incl. no tumour)

EfficientNetB0 trained on Kaggle Training, scored on Kaggle Testing (1,311 images): accuracy **96.7%**, balanced accuracy 96.5%.

| Test subset | Images | Accuracy in subset | Accuracy elsewhere | Fisher p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| test image has a near-copy in Training | 710 | 99.3% | 93.7% | 5.5e-09 |
| test image's patient is in Training | 171 | 97.7% | 96.6% | 0.64 |

## Do the explanations point at the tumour?

150 held-out images (114 patients), each explained by the fold model that never saw the patient, scored against the radiologist's tumour mask.

| | SHAP (expected gradients) | Grad-CAM |
|---|---|---|
| Median share of positive attribution inside the tumour | 3.5% | 2.5% |
| Median tumour area (chance level) | 1.2% | 1.2% |
| Median ratio to chance | 2.5× | 2.2× |
| Wilcoxon p (above chance) | 1.4e-25 | 2e-16 |
| Pointing game: peak inside tumour | 32.7% (chance 2.2%) | 20.0% (chance 2.2%) |
| Energy in tumour, correct vs wrong predictions | 3.3% vs 4.1% | 2.5% vs 2.4% |

Sanity check (randomly initialised model): rank similarity of maps trained vs random — SHAP 0.77, Grad-CAM 0.16 (low = the maps depend on what the model learned). Energy in tumour: trained 6.5% vs random 3.1%.
- SHAP: **does not pass** (similarity ≥ 0.5): the maps mostly reflect image structure, not what the model learned, so they should not be read as the model's reasoning.
- Grad-CAM: **passes** (maps change when the learned weights are removed).
SHAP completeness (sum of attributions vs model output change): r = 0.91.
